verdict.tagline: Dive by day and manage a sushi restaurant by night.
for_you_if: you enjoy combining ocean exploration with restaurant management
you appreciate charming pixel art aesthetics
you want an addictive loop that opens up over time
not_for_you_if: you dislike unskippable cutscenes in the opening hours
you are frustrated by losing inventory upon dying during dives
you need the ability to save mid-dive

This game is overhyped. It has so many issues, but the biggest one is the unskippable cutscenes, or all the way the game moves through things uncessecarily slow. Just launching from the boat is a good example. Cut scenes can't be skipped most of the time. The sushi game isn't even a game, it's just a weird time sucking experience (because it's not a game mind you). Have I mentioned unskippable cut scenes?

This game feels like I wasted my money and I don't know how much more of it I can take.

Since none of the other reviews seem to share my specific opinions, I'll put them out there. I found this game unenjoyable from the start, and quickly gave up. 

I like fish. I like the sea. I was excited to dive and see a beautiful, thriving environment with interesting, pretty fish. Maybe it gets better later on, but they are mostly, like, three pixels. They're not good depictions of fish, they are just depictions of the items you collect. It's not really about the fish, I guess. 

Then the restaurant part was immediately incredibly dull. Again, maybe this gets better, but it just felt like slowly waiting tables.

Then, they had me pull out a smartphone, screen full of apps that they are going to expect me to use, and told me to run an Instagram page to advertise the restaurant? To who??? There's nobody seeing it! This isn't real! Why do I have to do that? I wanted to play a game about having a job, not actually work a job. 

I never got far enough to be inundated with mini games as other reviewers are mentioning, but I already noticed that dialogue and non-gameplay matters were taking up too much time. I think I quit after like three ig days. 

Nothing that this game offered ended up being what I hoped, and I could find better versions of everything it claims to be somewhere else. 

Glad other people like it, though.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as combining daytime ocean exploration and fishing with nighttime sushi restaurant management.

citations.review_text:
I can't recommend this game enough! It's honestly one of the best games I've ever played.

Dave the Diver is an incredibly cozy game with a heartwarming story, beautiful pixel-art graphics, and an addictive yet relaxing soundtrack. During the day, you dive into the ocean to explore, catch fish, and uncover its mysteries. At night, you manage a sushi restaurant, creating a highly addictive gameplay loop that never gets old. The exploration feels rewarding, the characters are charming, and there's always something new to discover. It's the perfect balance between relaxing and engaging.

Once you start playing, it's incredibly hard to put down. If you're looking for a cozy, fun, and unforgettable experience, this game is an absolute must-play!

This game overrated as hell.

It started out really fun, you hunt for fish during the day and run a sushi restaurant at night but very quickly the game just starts throwing random task and sidequest at you to a point it's overwhelming. 

Navigation sucks, you never get clear direction to where to go. Tons of backtracking and fetch quests. It's just stop being fun after the 30th "new" idea they tried to throw your way, I really want to just keep progressing and see more of the story, too bad the game become tedious.

cohorts.summary: Deeper progression brings heavier stakes on death, missing save options during dives, and frustrating management systems.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that dying during a dive results in losing nearly the entire inventory except for a single selected item.

citations.review_text:
After finishing and getting the platinum for Dave The Diver it ended up being one of the most charming and genuinely fun games I’ve played in a long time. The game never takes itself too seriously, and that’s honestly its biggest strength, just when you settle into the gameplay loop, it throws some absurdly hilarious cutscene, random mini game, or over the top moment at you that somehow only makes the experience better. What surprised me most is how flexible the game is: you can focus almost entirely on diving, running the sushi restaurant, farming fish, completing side quests, taking photos, or cleaning the ocean floor, and each part feels satisfying enough to carry the game on its own. The characters are lovable, the animated scenes are packed with personality, and the atmosphere is fantastic. Despite the repetitive structure, the gameplay stays consistently engaging because every dive feels different depending on what fish, upgrades, or objectives you’re chasing. The diving can definitely get tense and frustrating at times; losing almost your entire inventory after dying is brutal, and sneaking past aggressive sharks sometimes feels like a stealth game, but that challenge adds real excitement and makes successful dives feel rewarding. 

Overall, Dave the Diver constantly balances humor, charm, challenge, and variety in a way that makes it incredibly hard to put down. 8.5/10

A surprisingly rich experience! I was expecting a casual diving-fishing game with a side of restaurant management sim, but there was quite a lot more to see. 
Following the story was fun. The characters, style, and frequent animated scenes are very charming and full of personality, some even getting a chuckle out of me with their silliness. 
I also didn’t expect to enjoy the soundtracks of some of the diving areas that much (Glacier Zone my beloved…)

Gameplay stays engaging despite the repetitive loop with each dives being different either looking for specific species of fish or items, as there is quite a decent number of side quests to do along the way. Diving itself was rather tricky and frustrating at times, with the penalty of loosing all your inventory but ONE item in case of failure being quite harsh. Sometimes it felt like a stealth game trying to get past overzealous sharks praying to stay unnoticed, but I guess it added a sense of challenge. 

For those who like the genre, I think it’s definitely a must play.

tldr; buy it, but beware of a few things

I like this game a lot. Amazing charm and super fun. The animations of this game matched with a consistent whimsey throughout shows how much love is in this game. I really enjoy the boss battles and their designs. Anything with a focus on fish and collecting them will always put me in a choke hold.  

HOWEVER, this game clearly is for an older audience but on so many occasions it holds your hands through puzzles that are so obvious. And then at other times you're confused by ui and what anything means. Does "send fish to fish tank" mean all my fish? Does "re dispatch" collect what my employees have procured or does it send them out again without collecting. There was a quest that mentioned you needed to go to a shipwreck so I obviously go to the shipwreck that we had a plot event at but no it's some random location that also is a shipwreck? With no map it's just a bit annoying to have this vague phrasing. There is no difficulty in puzzle gameplay but consistent difficulty with poor phrasing or unclear ui. 

Fishing in this game takes a lot of time. You will spend 90% of your game fishing and to be honest there is a little bit of dread every time I go into the ocean. This is because failure is very punishing. If you spend 30 mins collecting and fighting fish, and maybe are in a bad location so you can not get to an air tank or a quick snipe from an aggro fish, and you end up dying. You lose everything, besides one item you can choose. This has happened to me maybe 2-4 times maybe? It always makes me bad. It feels like I've wasted my time because it is such a time sink every time you go fishing. 

I don't know, I want to love this game but I do find myself groaning or gritting my teeth to try and get through everything because it feels like busy work a lot of the times.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game lacks the ability to save and quit while in the middle of a dive.

citations.review_text: This game is incredible, it's such a unique blend of so many types of gameplay that it never gets boring and you can tell that every detail is made with care. Everything is so chill and cozy even when I'm in a knife fight with a shark. My only complaint is that especially in late game, this becomes the king of long sequences where you can't open the menu to exit the game. I sometimes have a limited timeframe I am able to play and don't realize I am in an area where I can't open my menu for another 30 real life minutes.

Giving a no out of sheer pettiness to vent my irritation at several issues that have had me rage quitting many many times despite eventually getting through the difficulty.
Like the fact that there is no way to get to the load menu unless you go through the process of getting back to a place where you can use the cell phone. Its faster to force kill the process in task manager and restart the game if you are in a dive and something gets totally hosed up.
And I hate that fish and bosses can attack from above and below, but stupid fat Dave can only shoot 45 degrees up and down. So you VERY often get smacked around by fast enemies while you attempt to reposition your incredibly slow self level with them and far enough away to actually shoot.
Also I hate many of the the mini games, bosses and challenges because many are not beatable the first try unless you read a tutorial in advance or something online, either because it requires a specific complex strategy that isn't intuitive or the instructions for what to do outright suck and are often given to you to read right as a high speed challenge starts. By the time you figure out what they are talking about its too late. (I'm looking at you especially cooking challenges)
Just a tip for people stuck on one annoying part, the sneak into base mission if you keep getting spotted by the last guy before going up the ladder because the timing between the two guys wont let you move from behind the crates soon enough. Let the guy on the fridge/ladder side of the boxes half see you so he pauses, then quick hide until he moves again. That throws the timing between the two guys off so that you can hide in the fridge and make it up the ladder in time. That will all make sense when you are on that mission.

Otherwise its a good game with a nice classic vibe.

I love it! My main issue with this game though is that there's no way to save and quit when you're in the middle of a dive. Since dives are huge commitments, it ends up being a stressful experience where you have to weigh whether or not to commit to a potentially long dive. Guesstimating how long it will take, and sometimes the gamble kicks you in the butt.

I wanted to love this game, and it's quite cozy. If you just want to grind the core gameplay loop it will let you. But the rewards track suffers diminishing returns fast.
None of the harpoon mechanics feel very good. The sea people are insufferable and their fetch quests are intolerable. Restaurant management is the best element in my opinion, but there's not enough. Fish farming seems cool but when it can be unlocked there's already a lot of burnout suffered (especially if you get soft-locked at pulling out stakes and need to restart).
The music is great for the first 30mins but the same track playing every time you enter the water or manage the restaurant gets very very old. The jukebox functionality could be vastly more functional, meaning it could actually play the track you select while you play the game itself.
I may finish it at some point much later but overall a bit dissatisfying, after a compelling start.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the developer implemented the use of AI for translation, which negatively impacted their ability to support the project.

citations.review_text: Before the most recent update i would absolutely have recommended this game. However since the devs has decided to implement the use of AI in lieu of actual human translators has made me no longer able to support this project. A game that is largely about environmental conservation using a service that does more damage to the earth more than any other industry in history has a sad irony to it and i mourn this game that i once loved and put so much of my time into. Even if they do remove the AI from it they will still have used it in the first place and it is truly disheartening to have to see this.

One might assume that the capitol made off collaborations and crossovers from Dave the Diver would be able to cover the costs of human labor for a very nuanced part of media adaption. It is highly disappointing that the billion-won company cannot come to hire local translators and would resort to using AI translators. If I could refund the game, I would.
